Cayman Islands Industrial Intermediate Prod Trade Remains Steady in Q2

The Cayman Islands’ Industrial Intermediate Prod sector reported stable trade figures for the second quarter of 2024, according to data released Tuesday by the Department of Commerce and Industry. Imports and exports in the category, which includes processed materials used in manufacturing, showed modest year-on-year growth, with officials pointing to continued demand from regional partners.

According to the report, the total value of industrial intermediate goods imported into the Cayman Islands reached CI$23.4 million, up 2.1% from the same period last year. Exports saw a slight uptick as well, totaling CI$7.9 million, reflecting a 1.7% increase.

“Trade in intermediate products is an important barometer of our manufacturing sector’s health,” said Veronica Ebanks, Deputy Director at the Department. “The figures confirm ongoing stability, with no significant disruptions or fluctuations observed in the past quarter.”

Industry representatives echoed the positive outlook. “Local manufacturers continue to source the materials they need without interruption,” said Gregory Porter, president of the Cayman Industrial Association. “It’s business as usual, and the sector remains resilient.”

Analysts note that the figures align with broader Caribbean trends, as regional trade flows remain largely unaffected by global volatility. “Stable intermediate prod trade is a sign of underlying economic consistency,” said Alicia Morrison, an economist at Island Analytics.

Officials expect conditions to remain steady in coming months, with routine monitoring in place. The Department of Commerce and Industry plans to release its next quarterly update in September.
